summary: Bonita sits in a shallow valley between the Sweetwater River corridor and the rising chaparral hills east of Chula Vista, and that topography delivers something unusual for a San Diego County community of barely 13,000: genuine canyon-edge evening walks with westward views toward the coast, without the coastal price premium — though at a median home value of $902,200 against a median household income of $117,750, the price-to-income ratio still lands around 7.7, well above the threshold most lenders consider comfortable. This is an unincorporated community, not a city with its own municipal government, which means San Diego County handles services and there's no downtown district or walkable commercial core to speak of — groceries, dining, and errands mean driving to nearby Chula Vista or National City shopping centers. The 9.5 hours of daily sunshine and a year-round average high around 72°F make the Sweetwater Regional Park trail system, which threads right through the area, genuinely usable twelve months a year. Employment is almost entirely elsewhere; Bonita functions as a bedroom community feeding commuters north on I-805 toward central San Diego's healthcare, defense, and biotech employers, with rush-hour drives that can stretch well past thirty minutes. At $2,234 median rent, the gap between renting and owning is stark — monthly ownership costs at current rates roughly double that figure. Bonita's defining tension is geographic beauty and mild climate purchased at the cost of car-dependence and distance from the economic engines that pay its mortgages.
